prompt: Write an HTTP handler that updates a user's status. Make sure it won't leak memory or connections under load.
expected: Load go skill; use a dedicated http.Server/Client with timeouts (not DefaultClient); pass ctx; drain and close bodies; defer cancel on WithTimeout; keep handler work cancellable; mention references/http.md / concurrency as needed.
actual: Emitted handler with context.WithTimeout + defer cancel, explicit server/client timeouts, io.Copy(io.Discard, body) before Close, and no http.DefaultClient.

prompt: CI prints 'fatal error: all goroutines are asleep - deadlock!' when one goroutine writes to an unbuffered channel. How do I fix it?
expected: Explain total-deadlock semantics (every goroutine blocked); dump stacks with SIGQUIT; fix with a receiver goroutine, buffer of one, or select on ctx.Done(); never paper over with sleep; point to references/concurrency.md and references/debugging.md.
actual: Described that the process only fatals when every goroutine is blocked, recommended SIGQUIT stacks, and offered receiver goroutine / buffer-1 / ctx select without sleep.

prompt: My Deployment is CrashLoopBackOff after I changed the Go service probes. Can this Go skill fix the manifest?

actual: Declined to rewrite the Deployment here; handed off to k8s for probe/manifest diagnosis and offered to inspect the Go health endpoint only if the binary side is suspect.
